The process is. 👇 If you want to start selling digital products, here’s the simple step by step: 1️⃣ Pick ONE problem to solve Don’t create a random ebook and hope people buy it. Find a problem your audience already has. Examples: 🎨 “How do I use Canva?” 🐶 “How do I train my dog?” 🧘 “How do I build a better meditation routine?” The more specific the problem, the easier it is to create content around it. 2️⃣ Create a simple digital product 📕 You don’t need 100 pages. Create something that helps someone get from A → B. Think: ✅ Checklists ✅ Guides ✅ Templates ✅ Planners ✅ Workbooks ✅ Step by step instructions Your product should save someone time, confusion or frustration. 3️⃣ Create content that solves PART of the problem 🎥 This is where most beginners go wrong. They constantly say: “Buy my product!” Instead, teach. Give people something they can actually use. For example: ❌ “Buy my Canva guide.” ✅ “Here are 3 Canva mistakes making your designs look amateur.” Now you’re providing value AND attracting people who already have the problem your product solves. 4️⃣ Give them a reason to keep watching 👀 Use a simple structure: 🔥 Hook 📚 Value 🎯 Example 👉 Next step Example: “Your Canva designs look boring for one simple reason…” Then teach the reason. Show an example. Then tell them where they can learn the full process. 5️⃣ Post consistently 📈 You don’t need to be perfect. You need enough reps to learn what your audience responds to. Start with 1 piece of content per day. Then study: 👀 What gets watched? 💬 What gets comments? 🔄 What gets shared? 🔗 What gets clicks? 💰 What actually generates sales? Double down on what works. 6️⃣ Build trust before expecting sales 🤝 People don’t buy because you posted a link. They buy because they trust that you understand their problem and can help them solve it. Show: 📱 Your process 📚 What you're learning 🎥 Tutorials 💡 Tips 📊 Results 🧠 Mistakes you've made You’re not just selling a PDF. You’re selling a shortcut to a result. And remember… People can have opinions about what you’re doing. Let them. Your job isn’t to convince every person on the internet. Treat it like one. And remember: your legal protection shouldn’t start after someone steals or misuses your digital product. It should be part of your business from the beginning.
